title: Among length-aware B2, B3 and B4, which is the best robust throughput?
question: Among length-aware B2, B3 and B4 causal-KL execution, which protocol provides the best robust throughput on the real frozen workload, before paying for a full scorer?
_why_v1_was_not_enough: v1 ran ONE ordered pass and separated its two leading candidates by 0.76% (P2 252.614s, P3 250.686s) while their peak VRAM differed by 4.8 GiB (6.53 vs 11.30). Whichever protocol runs last has the warmer allocator, and that advantage is worth more than 0.76%. One obvious protocol, B3, had never been derived at all.
_v1_is_preserved: packing-optimization/v1 remains valid for the protocol it used: screen complete, P3 advanced under the v1 single-screen rule, full scorer not funded. Its 1.1581x / 1.1670x are historical CONTEXT and are NOT timing replicates in the v2 statistic.
_their_role_is_answered: v1 measured B2-consecutive at 1.0111x against B2-sorted at 1.1581x with the SAME invocation count, which is what established that packing rather than batch size is the variable.
_b3_needed_no_core_change: the packer and attention.causal_kl_v1 are parameterized in batch size. A `batch_size == 3` branch anywhere would be the defect, not the feature; a $0 test greps for one.

screen._why_these: early, middle and late depth; the model forward still traverses the whole model.
screen._counterbalanced: round B is the exact reverse of round A, so a position advantage in one round is a position disadvantage in the other and pooling cancels it. Frozen here before any timing.
screen._stability_guard: R0 is measured in both rounds. If |A-B|/mean(A,B) > 5% the environment cannot carry a sub-percent decision: STOP with TIMING_SCREEN_UNSTABLE. Do NOT add repeats opportunistically -- choosing the statistic after seeing the spread is choosing the result.
screen._near_tie_rule: candidates whose pooled wall is within 2% of the fastest are operationally TIED. Among tied candidates select by (1) lower peak VRAM, (2) then smaller calibration_forward_batch_size, (3) then lexical protocol id. Frozen before v2 timing, because a 0.5-1% fluctuation must not buy an execution mode that nearly doubles memory pressure.

full_scorer._fresh_b1_is_mandatory: v1 measured same-session P0 / scaled prior B1 = 1.2467x, far outside the preregistered +/-5% bound, so the 2190.1708s result CANNOT serve as a reference for a new speed claim. If v2 advances, a fresh full B1 and one full candidate run on the SAME session, card and runtime. No exception.
full_scorer._order_predeclared: before execution, and not chosen after the screen
full_scorer._same_contract: identical warm-up and CUDA synchronization as the screen
full_scorer._no_relaxation: the adoption threshold does not move because this is a third attempt

structural_comparison.reference: the verified landscape from the FRESH full B1 of this session
structural_comparison._not_layer_count_alone: a layer counts as changed if one slot in it differs; that measures spread, not magnitude.

recovery._rule: NOT AUTHORIZED IN v2. Even if the full speedup reaches 1.25x AND the head maps differ, STOP after the structural comparison and return for review.
recovery._why: budget and accounting clarity: first prove an execution protocol is worth adopting, only then spend on downstream-equivalence recovery.
recovery._seed_state: UNCONSUMED, and it stays unconsumed unless a later authorization explicitly uses it.

frozen_inputs._parent_reuse: search the durable store first; replay once at B1 only if the exact bytes are absent. ONE replay, and the same verified parent feeds every screen round and both full scorers.

aggregation_order._rule: execution may reorder; aggregation may NOT. Preserved from v1.
aggregation_order._how: per-item KL is written by original_item_index and aggregated by walking the frozen mixture from 0, so subtype accumulation, domain aggregation and item-to-score attribution are independent of the packing.

do_not_change: forward_kl_mean_batch chunk=512 -- a separate numerical variable
